sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The **Indus Valley Civilization (IVC)**, also known as the **Harappan Civilization**, is one of the world's oldest urban civilizations.
**Bronze Age** civilization flourishing roughly between **2500 BCE – 1750 BCE** (Radio-carbon dating by **D.P. Agrawal** estimates **2300 BCE – 1750 BCE**).
Spread across **North-Western India**, **Pakistan**, and **Afghanistan** in the river basins of the **Indus** and its tributaries.
Inhabitants were a multi-racial mix of **Mediterranean**, **Proto-Australoid**, **Mongoloid**, and **Alpine** stocks; first site discovered by **Dayaram Sahni**.
Pioneered **advanced urban town planning**, sophisticated **drainage systems**, **standardized weights and measures**, and trade networks.
**Grid system** of street layouts, **double-storied baked brick houses**, **Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro**, and **pictographic undeciphered script**.
High-scoring static GK area covering site locations, excavation years, archaeological findings, and river associations.
Belongs to **Proto-Historic Era** (Chalcolithic / Bronze Age); first to cultivate **cotton** (termed **Sindon** by Greeks).

items.title: Geographical Boundaries & Northernmost-Southernmost Points
items.content:
• **Northernmost Site:** **Manda** in Jammu & Kashmir on the banks of river **Chenab**.
• **Southernmost Site:** **Daimabad** in Maharashtra on the banks of river **Pravara**.
• **Westernmost Site:** **Sutkagendor** in Baluchistan on the banks of river **Dast**.
• **Easternmost Site:** **Alamgirpur** in Uttar Pradesh on the banks of river **Hindon**.
• **Mnemonic for Boundaries:** **"M-D-S-A = Mummy Drinks Sweet Apple"** (Manda, Daimabad, Sutkagendor, Alamgirpur).

items.title: Major Excavated Sites and Discoverers
items.content:
• **Harappa (1921):** Excavated by **Dayaram Sahni** on river **Ravi** (Montgomery district, Punjab, Pakistan).
• **Mohenjo-daro (1922):** Excavated by **R.D. Banerji** on river **Indus** (Larkana district, Sindh, Pakistan).
• **Chanhu-daro (1931):** Excavated by **N.G. Majumdar** on river **Indus**.
• **Kalibangan (1953):** Excavated by **A. Ghosh** on river **Ghaggar** (Rajasthan).
• **Lothal (1957):** Excavated by **S.R. Rao** on river **Bhogava** (Gujarat).
• **Dholavira (1990):** Excavated by **R.S. Bisht** in Kutch, Gujarat.

items.title: Town Planning and Architecture Features
items.content:
• **Grid System:** Cities divided into rectangular blocks with streets intersecting at right angles (90 degrees).
• **Two-Part Division:** Citadel (upper town for ruling elite) and Lower Town (for common citizens); **Dholavira** is uniquely divided into **three parts**.
• **Drainage System:** Covered underground drains made of mortar, lime, and gypsum with inspection manholes.
• **Building Material:** Dominant use of **standardized burnt bricks** (ratio length:breadth:height = 4:2:1).
• **Mnemonic for Unique Dholavira:** **"Dhol = 3 parts"** (Dholavira has three divisions unlike others).

items.title: Economy, Trade, and Agriculture
items.content:
• **Agriculture:** Chief crops included **wheat**, **barley**, **dates**, **mustard**, and **rice** (evidence from Lothal and Rangpur).
• **Domestication:** Rearers of **oxen**, **buffaloes**, **sheep**, **goats**, **pigs**, and **camels**; horses were known marginally (Surkotada).
• **Trade:** Extensive foreign trade with **Mesopotamia** (Sumeria); Indus seals found in Ur and Kish.
• **Imports:** Gold from Kolar (Karnataka), Silver from Afghanistan/Persia, Copper from Khetri (Rajasthan).
• **Weights & Measures:** Based on binary and decimal systems, multiples of 16 (e.g., 16, 64, 160).

items.title: Art, Craft, Seals, and Script
items.content:
• **Pashupati Seal:** Depicts a three-faced male deity (**Proto-Shiva**) surrounded by elephant, tiger, rhino, buffalo, and two deer at his feet.
• **Dancing Girl:** Famous **bronze** statue found in Mohenjo-daro crafted using the **lost-wax technique** (cire perdue).
• **Steatite Seals:** Mostly square-shaped featuring animal motifs and pictographic inscriptions.
• **Script:** **Boustrophedon style** (written right to left in the first line and left to right in the second); remains **undeciphered** till date.

items.definition: **H**arappa -> **D**ayaram (**H**d), **M**ohenjodaro -> **B**anerji (**M**b), **C**hanhudaro -> **M**ajumdar (**C**m), **K**alibangan -> **G**hosh (**K**g), **L**othal -> **R**ao (**L**r). Memorize as: **HD, MB, CM, KG, LR**.
Use the phrase **"Raja Ram Mohe Indus Pe Le"** -> **Ra**vi (Harappa), **Mohe**njodaro (Indus), **Le**j/Lothal (Bhogava). For Kalibangan: **"Kali Ghaghri"** (Kalibangan on Ghaggar).
Remember **MAPS**: **M**anda (North), **A**lamgirpur (East), **P**ravara/Daimabad (South), **S**utkagendor (West).
Use **G-S-C-T** -> **G**old (Kolar), **S**ilver (Afghanistan), **C**opper (Khetri), **T**in (Afghanistan/Iran).
Remember **TEER-B** -> **T**iger, **E**lephant, **E**lephant(2), **R**hino, **B**uffalo (and 2 deers at feet).
Fire altars are exclusively found in **Kalibangan** and **Lothal** (ritualistic/religious worship centers).

Students often think IVC people had **no knowledge of horses**. Correct fact: While horses were not central (unlike Vedic Aryans), evidence of horse bones is found at **Surkotada** and tooth remains at **Ranaghundai**.
Confusing IVC with Iron Age. Correct fact: IVC is a **Bronze Age** civilization. They **did not know about Iron**; iron was discovered later during the Vedic Period (around 1000 BCE at Atranjikhera).
Assuming large temples existed. Correct fact: **No temples or large places of worship** have been excavated in IVC; worship was nature and household/fertility-centric.
Confusing twin capitals. **Harappa and Mohenjo-daro** were designated as the twin capitals of the Indus empire by historian **Stuart Piggott**, not Lothal and Kalibangan.
Believing the Indus script has been read. Correct fact: The script remains **completely undeciphered**, despite numerous claims by epigraphists.
Assuming all cities had citadels. **Chanhudaro is the only major Indus city that lacked a citadel** (no fortified upper town).
IVC belongs to the **Proto-Historic period** and the **Bronze Age**, succeeding the Mehrgarh Neolithic culture.
Remarkable **grid iron pattern**, underground drainage, and advanced sanitary arrangements unmatched by contemporary civilizations.
First cultivators of **cotton** globally; grew wheat, barley, and used bullocks for plowing.
Extensive maritime and overland trade with **Mesopotamia**, **Persia**, and **Central Asia** using weights and measures.
Worshiped **Mother Goddess** (fertility), **Pashupati Mahadeva**, nature (peepal trees, animals like humped bulls), and fire.
Practiced **earth burial**, urn burial, and fractional burial; Lothal featured **double burials** (male and female together).
Mastery in **steatite seal carving**, terracotta figurines, bronze casting (lost-wax method), and bead manufacturing.
Decline attributed to **Aryan invasion** (Wheeler), **floods** (Marshall/Raikes), **tectonic disturbances**, or **desiccation of river Saraswati**.
Remarkable uniformity in brick sizes, weights, town layouts, and tools across distant settlements spanning 1.3 million sq. km.
UP sites include **Alamgirpur** (Meerut), **Hulas** (Saharanpur), and **Mandoli** (Ghaziabad), vital for state-level UPSSSC exams.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, focus heavily on matching **Sites with Rivers**, **Archaeologists**, and **Unique Findings** (e.g., Dockyard at Lothal, Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro).
Do not mark 'Cow' as a sacred animal worshipped on seals; the **Humped Bull** and **Pashupati** are prominent, but cows do not feature prominently on IVC seals.
Remember that Dholavira is famous for its unique **three-tier town planning** and stone architecture, unlike standard two-tier brick cities.
Be careful with questions asking about iron; IVC people were completely unaware of **Iron**, dealing exclusively in copper, bronze, gold, and silver.

keyTakeaways: IVC is a Bronze Age, proto-historic urban civilization dated between 2500 BCE and 1750 BCE.
Harappa (1921, Dayaram Sahni) and Mohenjo-daro (1922, R.D. Banerji) were the pioneer sites discovered.
Key urban features include grid-iron layouts, advanced covered drainage, and lack of temples/palaces.
Lothal served as the primary tidal dockyard facilitating maritime trade with Mesopotamia.
The Indus script is pictographic, written in boustrophedon style, and remains undeciphered.
UP sites like Alamgirpur (Hindon river) are high-yield areas for Uttar Pradesh competitive exams.
